scope: Synthetic process/shell controls only; no application test was rerun by this diagnostic.

observations.command:
set -e
trap 'scale_shell_exit=$?; printf "recorded-shell-exit=%s\n" "$scale_shell_exit"' EXIT
source /workspace/eduk12-cloud/load-local-env.sh
node -e 'process.exitCode=0'
scale_check_exit=$?
printf 'recorded-child-exit=%s\n' "$scale_check_exit"
exit "$scale_check_exit"

set -e
trap 'scale_shell_exit=$?; printf "recorded-shell-exit=%s\n" "$scale_shell_exit"' EXIT
source /workspace/eduk12-cloud/load-local-env.sh

observations.control: clear_console in the same noninteractive cloud login shell

conclusion: The synthetic check exits 0 in both cases. The login shell's explicit exit invokes ~/.bash_logout; its SHLVL=1 clear_console -q returns 1 with no console, and errexit makes the shell exit 1. Non-login shell records child=0, shell=0 and tool exit=0. This isolates the outer failure to login-shell cleanup. Historical child exit was not separately persisted; its successful progress past a standalone check under set -e and its real reporters are retained, not retroactively rewritten.

logoutFile.contents:
# ~/.bash_logout: executed by bash(1) when login shell exits.

# when leaving the console clear the screen to increase privacy

if [ "$SHLVL" = 1 ]; then
    [ -x /usr/bin/clear_console ] && /usr/bin/clear_console -q
fi
